purpose: Independent logical positive/reverse checks against static source and revised contracts; design only.

designs.premise_and_result: The revised body describes command choices, ordering factors, shared identities and observable failures without requiring the source choice record size, seven-entry ordering record, constructor wrapping, or inheritance layout. Necessary seat identifiers, input literals, data identity and alias effects remain. The registered B004/C006 root extensions remain allocated to their owners; this local finding is not a blanket ban on numbers or containers.
designs.reverse: Compare the removed layout assertions with retained selection/cancellation/order behavior; preserve a shared creature identity wherever it explains a real side effect. Unchanged protected N01 history is not a newly introduced architectural requirement.

designs.premise_and_result: In the qualified 3v3 layout, user seat 0 with dead ally 2 without a reserve and live ally 4 opens with 4 highlighted, no selected USE button, and may register 4. Execution still rejects the distant NearAlly target in the unchanged layout when no live nearby substitute exists. Display/registration permission and execution permission are different stages. The separate B033 residual remains with its owner.
designs.reverse: Revive ally 2: initial selection becomes 2. With both allies dead, the initial fallback is self 0. These reversals prevent inferring execution success from the selection screen.

designs.premise_and_result: Each experience share is floored before addition. The positive-base gate precedes trainer/scaled adjustments and the scaled +1; EV receipt remains an earlier independent effect. Integer division by 5 precedes scaling. The Caterpie level-2 base-39 / receiver-level-3 fixture gives 78, then 15, then 13 rather than 14. Subsequent charm, egg and affection truncations remain sequential.
designs.reverse: Two shares of 7/4 total 2 rather than flooring 7/2 to 3; nonpositive base does not gain the later +1, while prior EV receipt remains. The qualified 13 → 19 → 28 → 33 chain differs from applying all multipliers once (35).

designs.premise_and_result: Replacement opens the summary for the supplied creature with its four old moves and the new move, and returns an old-move slot or -1. It does not first select the first party member. A protected field move loops in nondebug mode; debug permits its selection. Choosing Back/new move leads to give-up confirmation: Yes leaves old moves intact and growth continues, No returns to selection. Battle learning refreshes PP and synchronizes the battler; machine PP retention is a separate consumer.
designs.reverse: Compare protected-move selection in debug/nondebug mode and give-up Yes/No. Preserve the same creature and the existing four moves on confirmed cancellation.

designs.premise_and_result: All six ordinary entry categories retain preset/map/global/default precedence. Trainer scanning keeps the last non-nil value, including an empty overwrite followed by fallback; the direct FromType entry may preserve an empty request and has no located fixed-Scripts caller. Intro preserves existing memorized audio, otherwise cancels and memorizes queued Q0, otherwise stores current audio/position or zero, before play. An empty intro request makes no audio-state change. Normal selection does not clear presets; normal transition return does. Overrides/skips do not acquire the normal consumer guarantees.
designs.reverse: Use two trainers with a later empty value to distinguish overwrite/fallback from first-nonempty selection; preserve preexisting memorized audio despite a queue. Capture ME requires no opponent remaining and retains the existing 3.5-second wait. No actual audio output is claimed.

designs.premise_and_result: A failure at the pre-PP precondition phase always clears last-used move and type, including a special use. A normal use also clears last regular move and target; a special use preserves that pair. PP remains unchanged. The candidate separates these outcomes from failures after PP consumption and does not promise transaction rollback.
designs.reverse: Use the same precondition failure with normal versus special use. Move the failure after PP consumption to verify it is outside the early-clear rule.

designs.premise_and_result: An existing NPC with a nonempty but fully fainted party passes the constructor existence/nonempty check, yet its sparse able-count collection can be empty. Start then fails the owner-count validation before the no-able message. A missing middle count with a later populated count passes the collection-length check and fails at the later comparison. Earlier start records and rule clearing remain committed; no implicit zero-fill or rollback is added. These are authored fixtures, not a claim about a bundled default trainer.
designs.reverse: Compare all-fainted existing trainer versus an able trainer; separately leave a middle owner count absent while a later one exists to distinguish the error phase.

designs.premise_and_result: The 14 rule literals retain their exact identities and distinct consumers. drawclause, modifiedselfdestructclause and suddendeath have consumers without a fixed facility setter wrapper; the generic sleep flag is not sleepclause. Skill Swap remains a common clause target gate. sleepclause checks existing party sleep with the actual origin distinction; self-induced sleep and modifiedsleepclause remain separate. Literal preservation describes compatibility, not an object architecture.
designs.reverse: Compare absent/true named clause, ordinary sleep setting versus sleepclause, and self-induced versus external sleep; do not infer consumer absence from a missing wrapper.

designs.premise_and_result: The revised rows supply the branch-determining premises: CP01 nonhit/disabled critical behavior; BC12 actual valid partner permission; CM05 earlier sleep/miss conditions; CM08 equal higher-priority ordering inputs; CM12 a live eligible non-primal creature. SW09 further requires an internal trainer battle, player owner 1, switch-style permission, a live current creature, no earlier switch, available backups, and no active Outrage. Ring absence or enemy count alone cannot determine the outcome.
designs.reverse: Negate a required premise at a time while keeping the remaining inputs fixed. The corresponding outcome must cease to be promised, rather than becoming an unspecified universal assertion.

designs.premise_and_result: ANY=false and FOREIGN=true are independent default settings, not a generation rule. With level 60 and badge-3 threshold 40, the player original creature does not enter this high-level RNG gate by default; a foreign creature does. Its draw 102 produces a=39 and passes this gate, while 103 produces a=40 and enters disobedience processing. This does not predetermine the later disobedience outcome. ANY=true also permits the original creature to enter; both flags false disable this high-level gate while Hyper Mode remains separate.
designs.reverse: Change only original/foreign status, or only ANY/FOREIGN flags; bracket the 102/103 draw boundary. Do not convert entry into disobedience processing into a fixed final action.

designs.premise_and_result: Weight uses 0.1 kg units, current form and temporary effects with a minimum of 1, then active ability (unless suppressed/Mold Breaker), then active item, again bounded below. Weight 1180 with active Light Metal becomes 590 and the qualified rate-45 example becomes 25 with capture x=8; suppression keeps 1180 and rate 45 with x=15. Float Stone has its own active-item gate. A 300 kg datum is 3000 units and takes +30 rather than the adjustment for the numeral 300.
designs.reverse: Compare active/suppressed ability and active/inactive item at otherwise identical boundaries. Existing zero-rate and weight-threshold rows remain preserved.

designs.premise_and_result: A valid registered consumable item with Direct5 battle use, no effect/qualification/condition handlers, and an eligible internal player/bag quantity 1 passes the default use qualification, registers, consumes 1→0, executes no effect, clears the choice, and receives no refund. Families 1/2 require an effect handler and family 3 requires its handler, so missing handlers reject before consumption. Family 4 is the dedicated ball path. The fixture is not an unknown item or proof of a default PBS item.
designs.reverse: Change Direct5 to each handler-requiring family while retaining the absent handler: reject with bag quantity 1. Add a valid handler only as a separate authored fixture.

designs.premise_and_result: The candidate identifies event value 2 as the event-touch trigger, rather than a display/priority condition. Trainer prefix, distance/reachability, jumping/over-trigger/current-event exclusions, A self-switch, unique second trainer and party capacity remain conditions. Static script eligibility does not establish a real map event chain.
designs.reverse: Change only the event trigger away from event-touch, or separately violate a remaining join condition; the second-trainer entry is no longer guaranteed.

designs.premise_and_result: At Perish count 1 on both sides, formal HP reaches 0 and fainting clears Flinch before the phase-14 checkpoint. With drawclause and the saved player-side singer, decision 2 returns early; Reflect remains 1 and endOfRound remains true because the later tail is skipped. Already committed faint cleanup is retained. A normal no-zero-Perish/decision-0 pass reaches wall expiry and endOfRound=false.
designs.reverse: Compare the early terminal Perish checkpoint with a nonterminal end phase. Preserve the difference between completed faint cleanup and skipped later cleanup, with no rollback claim.

designs.premise_and_result: ManualShift cancels the relevant multi-turn/Fury Cutter state but does not cancel stored Counter damage. Moving seats 0/2 preserves damage 20 and an enemy source seat 1, while independent other relation pointers to seats 0 and 2 are remapped. Manual movement consumes the actor action; automatic stage-23 adjustment is a different transition. Normal later end-phase counter clearing does not redefine the manual operation.
designs.reverse: Keep Counter source 1 while exchanging allied seats 0/2; separately use other pointers naming 0/2 to test remapping. Compare manual action cost with automatic adjustment and later counter reset.

designs.premise_and_result: Actual partner participation builds a combined battle party containing shared creature identities but a separate list from the player party. Removing and boxing A shifts player members and appends the catch without updating the old combined order. Terminal item restoration visits the old combined indexes: boxed A is still reached and restored to X; live B can be emptied there and later receive Y through the shifted player index, producing the specified anomaly. Without participation the synchronized party path leaves boxed A at its current item and restores live B from the shifted old record. Registered-but-nonparticipating partner is not a counterexample. The two approved clauses in each WP20 copy correctly separate exact same-participation restoration from the capture mismatch.
designs.reverse: Compare genuine participation, no partner and registered-only partner. For CP20 temporary Knock Off, use the qualified trainer Shadow/Snag Machine entry; wild-user Knock Off cannot establish that fixture. Without participation, retained A restores X but boxed A stays empty; permanent consumption nulls the old record and both remain empty. For middle member D, shifted E receives I_F and F receives nil while earlier members retain their records.

designs.premise_and_result: Damaging pivot uses a positive successful-hit count, not positive HP loss. The qualified physical U-turn against form-0 Eiscue with active Ice Face, no substitute/Mold Breaker, has HP loss 0 but a successful hit and can pivot if the user/reserve/opponent and original-unswitched-target gates still hold. This is not a promise for every absorption/reflection case.
designs.reverse: A miss yields no successful hit and no pivot. Negate user survival, eligible reserve, remaining opponent or the original-target condition to stop the guarantee despite the absorbed hit.

designs.premise_and_result: An available off-field future-attack source requires auxiliary battler initialization at the saved seat; that initialization clears other live relations naming this seat before it reads the saved source creature for the attack. A live B occupying source seat 0 can therefore lose its Mean Look relation on surviving target T at seat 1 when off-field A resolves. No formal switch is required. An on-field A uses the existing battler and does not perform fresh initialization. Empty/fainted target and unavailable source return earlier; they do not promise this cleanup.
designs.reverse: Compare A off-field versus already on-field, with the same live T and relation to seat 0. Reverse target/source availability separately to establish the earlier-return boundary.

designs.premise_and_result: The four-round noninternal Lapras fixture uses level 60, Water Absorb, no held items, HP 226, and neutral speeds 89/77. Player Perish Song first, then Growl while the opponent uses Growl, leaves the saved singer on player seat 0 while the last mover is opponent seat 1. At simultaneous expiry, drawclause yields checkpoint 2 and the noninternal continuation preserves it. Swapping the singer to the opponent gives checkpoint 1; changing only the final mover keeps checkpoint 2. Ordinary self-KO decisions based on the last user remain player=1, opponent=2, unknown=5. General intermediate checkpoints may still be overwritten where explicitly permitted.
designs.reverse: Swap only the singer, then separately swap only the final mover; preserve the distinction from ordinary self-KO. Lapras data/stats are static prerequisites, not observed rounds.

designs.premise_and_result: Stage 23 collects side-0 then side-1 plans from the preadjustment live layout. A near pair breaks collection but preserves earlier plans; single-seat sides are skipped and same-owner constraints apply. Real exchanges require both existing endpoints and the same owner. If multiple plans exist, only plans for a two-seat side are skipped; three-seat plans continue, without a new proximity check after the first exchange. Thus 3v3 with only 0/1 live yields 2/3, while 3v2 yields 2/1. A legal three-owner player versus one-owner opponent layout yields 0/3 rather than relying on the prohibited two-multi-owner layout.
designs.reverse: With 1v3 and only 0/5 live, move 5→3; already-near 0/3 produces no plan. Missing-endpoint cases are direct static malformed fixtures. An earlier return that never reaches stage 23 makes no automatic-adjustment promise.

scalar_arithmetic_checks.method: Independent Decimal scalar arithmetic at precision 80, not reference code or battle/vector execution.
